To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the skin of the fingers, palm, toes and soles can be used for non-invasive assessment, and that forearm Tsk can be used to assess the perfusion of these regions.
skin temperature is related to perfusion in the digits, but in the rest of the limbs, it is related to the arterial inflow.
The skin temperature of the hand is a good indicator of the perfusion of both the hand and the forearm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of skin temperature as a non-invasive measure of limb perfusion.
the thermal properties of the skin and its blood supply in the limbs.
the thermal properties of the skin of normal limbs and their relationship with the circulation of the limb as a whole.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the relationship between skin temperature and skin blood flow is not a simple one and is dependent upon the temperature of the ambient air and the temperature of the arterial blood supply to the limbs, the site of the skin being monitored, the site and nature of any exercise being undertaken and the nature of the disease affecting the limb.
skin temperature in the hand and feet is a measure of the perfusion of their glabrous skin and that of the forearm and calf is related to the inflow to the limbs.
the relationship between Tsk and perfusion of the skin is complex and depends upon the site of measurement and the environmental conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Tsk can be used to measure skin perfusion in the digits but not the forearm or calf and that the relationship between Tsk and perfusion depends on the relative importance of conduction and perfusion in maintaining Tsk.
Tsk of the skin of a limb is determined by the perfusion of that skin and by the heat conduction from the limb's thermal core.
the skin temperature is a function of its perfusion, of the temperature of the underlying tissues, and of the ambient conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

skin temperature is a good indicator of perfusion in the digits and that the perfusion of other parts of the limbs can only be assessed by measuring the Tsk in the digits and using the relationship between them.
the relationship between skin temperature and skin perfusion is not straightforward.
the skin temperature is a good indicator for the skin perfusion of the fingers, palm or toes.
